# Spool documentation corpus

Generated from repository-owned documentation on 2026-07-29.
Third-party documentation text is not reproduced. External products are named
only where needed to describe Spool integrations.

## Documentation conventions

Spool is an open-source, self-hostable print control plane and local print-node
agent. Repository-relative Markdown links include the literal `.md` extension
so they work in source archives, raw Markdown readers, and GitHub. External
links use full HTTPS URLs. Credentials, signed URLs, native profile blobs, and
unredacted support data never belong in URLs.

Status terms are evidence claims:

- Implemented: code exists in the repository.
- Tested: the named automated or physical test actually ran.
- Preview: evaluation is possible but release gates remain.
- Supported: a stable published support tier covers the behavior.
- Disabled: development-only and not a production release claim.
- Planned: design only.

The release support matrix is authoritative. At generation time, macOS and
Linux native paths are Preview and Windows is Disabled for production. Native
archives are unsigned. Source implementation, automated tests, an ad-hoc
physical test, and stable support certification are different facts.

## Product model

Spool accepts print jobs from a native API or a PrintNode-shaped compatibility
API, stores durable tenant/job state in PostgreSQL, stores content in an
S3-compatible object store, and routes work to an enrolled node. The node
persists accepted work in SQLite, uses an isolated executor, and hands output
to CUPS or the Windows spooler through installed local drivers.

Durable edges:

    integration
      -> control plane / PostgreSQL / S3
      -> enrolled node / SQLite
      -> executor
      -> OS spooler
      -> physical printer

PostgreSQL coordinates tenant state, job idempotency, leases, routing, event
history, and transactional outboxes. Object storage holds document content.
The node owns native printer discovery, driver access, local recovery, and
opaque native profile blobs. Tray/menu applications are disposable clients of
an authenticated loopback API; they do not own queues or device credentials.

## Deployment journeys

### Local-only

Local-only mode runs the headless agent, durable node queue, executor, and
loopback API on one computer. The API defaults to 127.0.0.1:39100 and requires
the generated local.token for operational routes. It is an API, not an embedded
web page. Local-only mode has no remote submission, multi-node routing, hosted
identity, or off-device recovery.

### Docker Compose

The evaluation topology runs spool-server, PostgreSQL 16, and MinIO. The
dashboard is optional. Operators replace every placeholder, keep bootstrap
keys server-side, pin production images by digest, and back up PostgreSQL and
objects as one logical set. This topology is not highly available.

### Kubernetes

The production Helm foundation requires external PostgreSQL and S3. It renders
api, sync, and worker Deployments; a migration job; optional dashboard; HPA;
PDB; topology spreading; anti-affinity; probes; restricted security contexts;
NetworkPolicies; service accounts; External Secrets integration; and Ingress
or Gateway API routing.

The current server binary is combined-role. All three pools still expose HTTP
and run PostgreSQL-leased background work. The pools provide scaling and
failure boundaries, not code-level role isolation. Production requires
database HA/PITR, object retention/replication, immutable images, secrets, TLS,
WAF/rate limits, monitoring, and rehearsed failover.

### GCP foundation

Terraform defaults to Sydney Cloud Run with external PostgreSQL and S3.
Optional resources add warm Melbourne compute, a global HTTPS load balancer
with bounded 5xx outlier detection, regional-HA Cloud SQL with a Melbourne read
replica, and Sydney/Melbourne dual-region objects. Managed data resources are
not automatically wired into runtime secrets. Database promotion, credentials,
cutover, fencing, and reconciliation remain explicit operator actions.

No repository configuration is itself a public Supported Spool SaaS.

## Node journeys

### Pairing

Interactive nodes generate their Ed25519 identity locally and use a ten-minute,
single-use browser approval. The approval page shows non-secret node metadata
and requires the eight-character code displayed by the node. The human web
session is never stored on the node. Headless automation can use a short-lived
enrolment token through protected input; enrolment secrets do not belong in
arguments, filenames, URLs, analytics, or logs.

### macOS

The source implements CUPS discovery/submission, local durability,
authenticated status, a native menu, PrintCore capture, immutable profile
revisions, and headless PrintCore replay. Add/Edit opens the actual macOS print
panel and captures settings without printing. The release tier is Preview:
artifacts are unsigned/not notarised and formal packaging/hardware matrices
remain.

### Windows

The source implements tray status/printer/profile menus, the driver's genuine
DocumentPropertiesW property sheet, full public/private DEVMODE capture, and
PDFium-to-GDI replay foundations. A Windows node talks to its own loopback
agent, not a Mac's 127.0.0.1. Nodes meet through the control plane. Windows
remains Disabled for production while signing, service lifecycle, installer,
physical PDF/RAW, complex-driver, restart, and reliability gates remain.

### Linux

The source implements CUPS discovery, PDF/RAW submission, durable local
queuing, authenticated loopback control, executor supervision, systemd
templates, and an optional small status tray. Listed x86-64 distributions and
Linux ARM64 remain Preview pending packaging/hardware evidence.

### Updates and diagnostics

Node upgrades are operator-managed. Drain work, preserve delivery-uncertain
evidence, back up state/identity, verify artifacts from a trusted channel,
replace binaries, verify queues/profiles, and canary print. Checksums are not
code signing. Fully automated signed native updating is not Supported.

Diagnostics include version, OS/architecture, node/job/printer/profile IDs,
timestamps, state events, native spooler correlation, redacted logs, and driver
version. A complete one-click support-bundle export is Planned. Never include
API/enrolment/local tokens, device keys, database URLs, signed object URLs,
documents, native blobs, full DEVMODE/PrintCore state, or customer labels.
Review and encrypt any support archive and set a retention deadline.

## Printing model

### Printers

A logical printer belongs to a node and points at an exact native queue ID.
Display names are not identifiers. Multiple nodes may expose equivalent
physical devices as distinct destinations. One physical device may use
multiple deliberate OS queues, but immutable profiles are preferred when the
driver reliably restores saved state.

### Native profiles

A profile is a named immutable revision for one exact queue and driver
fingerprint. It includes safe portable summaries, an opaque node-local native
blob, stock/dependency metadata, allowed per-job overrides, validation/test
state, and publication state. Edit restores an exact revision and creates a
new revision; Clone creates a new identity. Jobs pin an exact revision.

Native blobs are not recreated or edited in the web UI. Driver, queue, port,
firmware, or device changes may stale a profile. Structural validation is not a
physical print test.

### Complex drivers

Manufacturer-specific settings such as stock sensing, gap/black mark,
registration, white toner, feed direction, cutter, tray, and finishing remain
in the genuine vendor driver UI. Spool saves opaque native state rather than
cloning every option. Profiles must be qualified on the final node, queue,
driver, firmware, device, stock, and loading procedure. Only explicitly safe
fields such as copies/pages should remain per-job overrides.

### Queue layers

The control plane durably registers jobs/content/profile pins and waits for a
node. The node SQLite queue protects already accepted/downloaded work through
network interruptions. CUPS or Windows owns the native job after handoff. New
work waits or expires while a node is offline; accepted local work may continue.
An ambiguous handoff becomes delivery_uncertain and is never blindly retried.

### Job states

Typical progression:

    registered -> content_pending -> waiting_for_agent -> agent_downloading
    -> agent_accepted -> queued_local -> preparing -> rendering
    -> spool_intent -> accepted_by_spooler -> spooling -> printing
    -> completed_reported

Terminal/intervention states also include cancelled, expired, failed_retryable,
failed_terminal, and delivery_uncertain. accepted_by_spooler does not mean paper
exited. completed_reported is the strongest reported completion, not
independent physical proof.

## API model

Native clients use:

    Authorization: Bearer spl_...

Keys are server-side secrets, one per integration/environment, with minimum
scopes. Bootstrap credentials are rotated after durable keys exist. Nodes use
their enrolled identity. Hosted OIDC verifies issuer, JWKS, application
binding, organization, and permission claims; unrestricted OIDC remains off.
PrintNode compatibility routes use HTTP Basic with the compatibility key as the
username and an empty password.

Native job registration is POST /v1/jobs. Clients send an Idempotency-Key of
8-255 characters. The same key and request returns the recorded job; the same
key with a different request returns idempotency_conflict. Idempotency prevents
duplicate registration, not ambiguous physical delivery.

Job content can reference an upload, Base64 data, or a URI. URI content must
remain available until node download; private/short-lived content should use
uploads. A successful create is durable registration, not printing.

Webhook endpoint management, encrypted signing secrets, transactional outbox,
retry history, and replay are implemented. Delivery is at least once. Spool
signs the exact raw body with HMAC-SHA256 over:

    <decimal timestamp>.<raw body>

Headers are Spool-Timestamp and Spool-Signature: v1=<base64>. Consumers verify
before parsing/side effects, use constant-time comparison and a timestamp
tolerance, durably deduplicate event IDs, and return 2xx only after acceptance.

The PrintNode-shaped API implements computers, printers, print jobs, states,
cancellation, and compatibility authentication/idempotency with documented V1
bounds. Collections currently hydrate bounded windows in some routes. Scales,
integrator/child-account headers, and exact undocumented race behavior are not
claimed as parity.

## Operations

### Configuration

Secrets come from protected files/stores, not Git, images, URLs, logs, or
support data. Separate staging/production state. Pin immutable artifacts.
Hosted environments keep unrestricted OIDC and plain HTTP object access off.
Preserve node data, identity, profiles, and delivery evidence across changes.

### Upgrade

Back up, stage, run compatibility tests, execute migrations, roll server
replicas behind readiness, observe, then canary nodes. Server comes before
agents. Migrations remain compatible with the previous server during rolling
windows. Do not combine driver replacement with a Spool rollout unless profile
invalidation is planned and tested.

### Backup/restore

Back up PostgreSQL and objects as one logical set with PITR, object versioning,
separate failure domains, encryption, documented RPO/RTO, and restore drills.
Restore in isolation with printing/webhooks blocked; verify migrations,
digests, tenants, events, idempotency, outboxes, and profiles; then canary.
Preserve node/native queues and reconcile uncertain deliveries.

### High availability

Replicas share PostgreSQL/S3 and coordinate with leases/outboxes. Spread at
least two replicas across nodes/zones and gate traffic on readiness. Regional
compute failover cannot make a database writable. Fence writers before
cross-region database promotion, rotate the connection secret, reconcile lag,
and rehearse failback. Replication is not a zero-RPO guarantee.

### Monitoring

Monitor API latency/errors/readiness; job depth/oldest age/retries/expiry/
delivery_uncertain; node heartbeat/printer warnings/profile mismatch/native
queue; PostgreSQL latency/connections/locks/replication; object integrity; and
webhook backlog. /v1/health is process liveness. /v1/ready gates PostgreSQL and
object readiness. Neither proves physical output.

### Incident response

Declare ownership/severity/timeline, preserve evidence, stop expansion, classify
waiting/failed/uncertain jobs, and rotate exposed credentials. Never bulk retry
ambiguous output. Reconcile Spool ID, native ID, physical output, and stock.
Fence database writers before promotion. Share only redacted support data.

## Contributor model

The toolchain uses Rust 1.88, Node 22, pnpm, Swift on macOS, Docker, and
platform print dependencies. Ordinary tests never physically print. The full
suite covers formatting, strict Clippy, Rust tests, web tests/checks, and Swift
tests when available. Physical certification is separately authorized with a
named printer, stock, expected output, and retained evidence.

Architecture changes preserve durable ownership, crash behavior, tenant scope,
profile pins, native blob locality, protocol compatibility, and duplicate/
timeout/restart tests. Material public protocol, security, durability, native
format, dependency, and support-tier changes use an RFC and normally an ADR.
RFC acceptance does not change a release support tier; evidence gates do.
